heading: The work, not the numbers.
intro: Awards are what other people notice. This is what Nahim actually does, and who it’s for.

areas.title: Detached youth work
areas.blurb: Going to the corners and estates where young people actually are, at the hours they’re there. Often in his own time. This is where most of the trust gets built.

areas.title: Employment and training
areas.blurb: A big part of Nahim’s frontline work has been getting under-25s onto courses and into jobs — sometimes by walking them through the door himself.

areas.title: Spotlight
areas.blurb: Poplar HARCA’s award-winning youth service for 11 to 19 year olds in Tower Hamlets. Nahim went from engagement manager to leading strategic engagement across youth and community.

areas.title: Violence reduction
areas.blurb: Spotlight is part of the MyEnds consortium supported by London’s Violence Reduction Unit. Nahim has spoken alongside the Mayor of London on the funding frontline youth work needs.

areas.title: Prevention and awareness
areas.blurb: Workshops with young people on the risks in front of them, from nitrous oxide to anti-social behaviour, delivered where they are rather than where it’s convenient.

areas.title: Speaking up for the sector
areas.blurb: On panels, in the press and in webinars with policymakers, making the case that youth work has been underfunded and undervalued for a decade, and what to do about it.

caseStudies.title: One course, one job
caseStudies.challenge: A young man in Poplar with no clear route into work, and a four-day security industry course he was unlikely to finish on his own.
caseStudies.what: Nahim went out of his way to get him through it — the practical stuff, the encouragement, the showing up.
caseStudies.happened: He completed the course and got a job. He’s now looking ahead rather than back.
caseStudies.learned: It’s rarely the course that’s the barrier. It’s having one adult who will see it through with you.
